title: The years-overdue announcement post for FlickBoard | natkr's ramblings
excerpt: (Or: How I fell into the (mobile) keyboard rabbit hole.)
content_html:
(Or: How I fell into the (mobile) keyboard rabbit hole.)

I don't really call myself a keyboard nerd.

I use a plain old QWERTY12 keyboard. The swedish version.3 It's probably not optimal, but it works well enough for me. At least well enough that I haven't really had a reason to learn anything else.4

Except.. I do have this one dirty secret. You see, I really don't like it when computers tell me how, or what, to write.5 I just want to press a key, and see that letter show up on the screen, goddamnit.

That's.. fine on a desktop computer.

It's how most keyboards and applications work there!6 At most,7 you'll get a red squiggle if it doesn't like the word, or maybe a green one if it doesn't like how you put them together. And usually that's at least pretty easy to turn off in some menu option somewhere,8 so I can get my calm back.

But phones don't really work like that.9

The screens are tiny. Try to squeeze twelveish keys into a single row, and they end up downright microscopic. And you can't even feel the edges between the keys, since it's all just a flat sheet of glass.10

So, you pretty much have to cheat to make QWERTY usable there at all.11

If the thing you typed almost looks like a word, why not just.. fix it for you. In fact, if you know the start of the word, you can adjust the size of the keys to make it easier to hit the letters that it expects you to type.

Hell, forget all about that whole tapping business at all. If you do one swipe over the letters, that's probably enough to dig up some words that look right.

As long as the words you're looking for are in the dictionary.

Ducking awesome, init?12

Personally, I'm not so keen on that future.13

But.. does QWERTY still make sense here?

Touch screens may take away our space and tactility, but they do give us things back in return. We can do gestures now!14

Could we use this to pack the letters together a bit tighter, and make the keys bigger instead? Surely that should make it easier to hit the right one.15

Well, yeah. If you just consider the basic directions, you now have 9 unique interactions16 for one button that are still pretty easy to do and distinguish!

Take a 3x3 grid of those buttons, and you've got more than plenty to squeeze in the whole latin alphabet, and then some.

So some people made a layout and keyboard based on that principle, called MessagEase:

It never really got beyond a fairly small niche17, but it worked pretty well! Finally,18 I could type on my phone, without all the cheating!19

But the good times couldn't last.

ExIdeas (the company behind MessagEase) is a corporation, after all.

And a few years ago, they altered the deal. No more typing for you. At least not until you hand over your credit card.

And I understand the need to pay rent. But I also think it's pretty shitty to hold people's decade+ of muscle memory hostage like that.

It really be all that expensive in the grand scheme of things, but the principle of the thing pissed me off. And if they can put it behind a paywall, they can take it away entirely too.20

So, uh, how hard could it be to do it yourself, anyway?

So, uh, yeah. I guess I fell into the keyboard rabbit hole, after all. Oops.21 Though it's been a few years at this point.22

If you want to try it out, it's called FlickBoard.

You can check out the code, or try it out immediately. And this time it's licensed under the AGPL, which means that I can't just take it away because I feel like it (though you can't, either).23

If you're used to MessagEase already then it should hopefully feel pretty familiar.

If you haven't tried a MessagEase-like keyboard before, I'm hoping that it's still a pretty soft landing. It'll take some getting used to any new layout, though.

And either way, feel free to hit us up if something doesn't look right! (Or poke us anyway if it does!)

  1. If you don't know what that is, it's probably the layout of your current keyboard! It's named that because, well, those are the first six letters of it. ↩

  2. Sorry, Dvorak fans.24 ↩

  3. Yes, that means that semicolon and slash are hidden behind shift, and that square brackets require altgr. ↩

  4. Well, I guess I did finally learn how to type loadkeys sv-latin1 on US-QWERTY without stumbling around for the dash, so there's that... ↩

  5. I've had that opinion since before the LLMania, but it certainly hasn't exactly mellowed that opinion. ↩

  6. With apologies to anyone using transliteration-based input methods. I don't speak any languages that require that, so I don't have any experience with them. ↩

  7. Glares at Microslop and Google for trying to change that, though... ↩

  8. At least there aren't any tigers to beware of! ↩

  9. At least not the modern slate phones. Remember when "smartphone" meant you could just slide out a keyboard? ↩

  10. Or plastic. Or some other transparent mineral. ↩

  11. If you want to try "true" touch QWERTY on an Android phone, Hacker's Keyboard is a bit of an eye-opener. ↩

  12. With apologies to Watterson, I think verbing is pretty great, actually.25 ↩

  13. Or present. ↩

  14. Like the swipe example from before, heh. ↩

  15. Thanks, Fitts. ↩

  16. Taps, swipes towards the four edges, and four corners. ↩

  17. How many people are willing to go back to barely being able to type for like a month, until they get used to it again? ↩

  18. I'm fudging the order a bit here based on my own experiences with it all. According to Wikipedia, MessagEase was released in 2002, a year before Android was founded in 2003. Let alone when Apple popularized slates-with-touch-keyboards in 2007. ↩

  19. MessagEase did still contain an autocorrecter, but at least it was usable without it. ↩

  20. To go back to Swype, that certainly didn't have a pretty end. ↩

  21. At least it's cozy down here. ↩

  22. How late is too late to write the announcement post? ↩

  23. Though I absolutely understand that this still isn't really enough on its own to be me-proof, either. Just look at the current situations around Linus or Mozilla. After all, having the code doesn't mean that it doesn't take time and skill to actually get familiar with it. But I think it's still the bare minimum to do. ↩

  24. Sorry, Colemak fans.26 ↩

  25. I wonder if verbing is in the dictionaries these days?27 ↩

  26. Sorry, Neo fans.28 ↩

  27. Looks like at least Merriam-Webster says yes! ↩

  28. Sorry, anyone who actually enjoyed this bit.29 ↩

  29. See, this doesn't even go anywhere anymore!30 ↩

  30. Unless?31 ↩

  31. No, I think we're finally done.32 ↩

  32. Slutstation, vi ber samtliga passagerare att stiga av samt kontrollera att inga värdesaker glömts kvar. ↩

content_html_zh:
（或者：我是如何掉进（移动）键盘兔子洞的。）

我并不真正称自己为键盘迷。

我使用普通的老式 QWERTY12 键盘。 瑞典版本。3 它可能不是最佳的，但对我来说已经足够好了。 至少足够好，以至于我没有真正理由去学习其他任何东西。4

除了.. 我确实有这个肮脏的秘密。 你看，我真的不喜欢计算机告诉我如何写或写什么。5 我只想按一个键，然后看到那个字母出现在屏幕上，该死的。

那是.. 在台式电脑上很好。

这就是大多数键盘和应用程序的工作方式！6 最多，7 如果它不喜欢这个词，您会得到一个红色的曲线；如果它不喜欢您将它们组合在一起的方式，您可能会得到一个绿色的曲线。 通常，这至少很容易在某个菜单选项中关闭，8这样我就可以恢复平静。

但手机实际上并不是这样工作的。9

屏幕很小。 尝试将十二个键挤成一排，它们最终会变得非常微小。 您甚至感觉不到按键之间的边缘，因为它只是一块平板玻璃。10

因此，您几乎必须作弊才能使 QWERTY 在那里可用。11

如果您输入的内容几乎看起来像一个单词，为什么不直接.. 为你解决它。 事实上，如果您知道单词的开头，则可以调整按键的大小，以便更轻松地敲击它希望您键入的字母。

见鬼，完全忘记整个攻丝业务。 如果你在字母上滑动一下，可能就足以找出一些看起来正确的单词。

只要您要查找的单词在词典中即可。

闪避太棒了，init?12

就我个人而言，我不太热衷于那个未来。13

但.. QWERTY 在这里还有意义吗？

触摸屏可能会夺走我们的空间和触觉，但它们确实给了我们一些回报。 我们现在可以做手势了！14

我们可以用它来将字母包装得更紧一些，并使按键更大吗？ 当然，这应该会让你更容易找到正确的目标。15

嗯，是的。 如果您只考虑基本方向，现在一个按钮就有 9 种独特的交互16，而且仍然很容易做到和区分！

采用这些按钮的 3x3 网格，您就可以挤入整个拉丁字母，甚至更多。

于是有人根据这个原理做了一个布局和键盘，叫做MessagEase：

它从未真正超越一个相当小的利基市场17，但它运作得相当好！ 最后，18 我可以在手机上打字，无需作弊！19

但美好时光并没有持续多久。

毕竟，ExIdeas（MessagEase 背后的公司）是一家公司。

几年前，他们改变了交易。 不再为您打字。 至少在您交出信用卡之前不会。

我理解需要支付租金。 但我也认为像这样扣押人们十多年的肌肉记忆是非常糟糕的。

从宏伟的计划来看，它确实是那么昂贵，但它的原理让我很生气。 如果他们可以将其置于付费墙后面，他们也可以将其完全拿走。20

那么，呃，自己做到底有多难呢？

所以，呃，是的。 我想我毕竟掉进了键盘兔子洞。 哎呀。21 虽然现在已经过去几年了。22

如果你想尝试一下，它的名字叫FlickBoard。

您可以查看代码，或立即尝试。 这次它是根据 AGPL 获得许可的，这意味着我不能因为我喜欢就将它拿走（尽管你也不能）。23

如果您已经习惯了 MessagEase，那么它应该会感觉非常熟悉。

如果您之前没有尝试过类似 MessagEase 的键盘，我希望它仍然是一个相当软的着陆。 不过，需要一些时间来适应任何新的布局。
